Choose the appropriate classification technique (sensitive information type, exact data match, or trainable classifier) to meet a requirement while minimizing false positives.
Recognize how Microsoft Purview reporting verifies that classification is being applied as specified.
Verify that classification and labeling support safe Microsoft Copilot grounding.
keyPoints: **SIT** detects a predictable *shape* (regex, keywords, proximity, checksum). **EDM** matches against a hashed reference table (up to 100 million rows, daily refresh). A **trainable classifier** learns from examples for free-form content.
SITs, trainable classifiers, EDM SITs and document fingerprinting can all drive **auto-labeling**; combining a classifier with a custom SIT can sharpen precision.
**Item scope** (Files & other data assets, Emails, Meetings) protects the content wherever it goes. **Groups & sites** scope protects the container only and doesn't label or encrypt the items inside.

A label scoped only to Groups & sites isn't shown in Office apps. **Container labeling must be enabled** tenant-wide before its settings can be configured. Meetings scope needs Files & other data assets.
Overlapping label policies give the **union of labels**, but conflicting **settings** resolve to the single highest-priority policy (highest order number); they never merge.
Two orderings: **label-policy priority** (which settings win) vs. **label-list priority** (ranking for downgrade detection and auto-labeling match resolution).

**Content explorer** = what is classified now (encrypted labels don't show for SharePoint/OneDrive). **Activity explorer** = changes over time, up to 30 days. Viewing the tab and viewing content need different permissions.
Copilot needs **VIEW and EXTRACT** rights, inherits the highest-ranked label, can't use **DKE** content, and has gaps for Teams meeting/channel chat labels and container labels.

units.title: Choose a classification technique for a data shape
points: SIT: consistently formatted data; confirms shape, not that a value belongs to a real record.
EDM: fixed enumerable list such as an account roster; hashed table, not shared with anyone including Microsoft; precision still depends on schema and validation.
Trainable classifier: varied free-form content such as case files, learned from examples.
EDM SITs support service-side (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online) and client-side auto-labeling.

units.title: Exercise - Create a custom sensitive information type for Woodgrove's transaction pattern
points: Create under Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types with a regular expression primary element at Low confidence.
A supporting element such as a nearby keyword helps before moving to a higher confidence level.
Test with the SIT tester, one unencrypted file at a time: one file that should match, one with near-misses.

units.title: Design what a sensitivity label protects
points: Item scopes: Files & other data assets (default), Emails (with attachments), Meetings (calendar events, Teams meeting options, chat).
Groups & sites controls privacy, external sharing, unmanaged device access, discoverability and shared channels.
A single label can carry both item and container scope, but that is a deliberate choice.
Container settings are grayed out until container labeling is turned on.

units.title: Publish label policies and resolve conflicting settings
points: A label reaches users only through a published label policy (labels shown, default label, mandatory labeling, justification on removal/downgrade).
Ways to apply: manual, default, mandatory (a requirement, not a selection), recommended, automatic (service-side supports SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online).
Conflicting settings: only the highest-priority policy applies; fix by reordering with Move up / Move down.
Policy priority is set on the Label policies page; label-list priority on the Labels page.

units.title: Exercise - Configure and publish a sensitivity label policy, then verify priority resolution
points: Create an item-scoped label with encryption and a content marking footer; needs Sensitivity Label Administrator or Information Protection Admins.
Publish with justification on downgrade, mandatory labeling and a default label.
A second lower-priority policy doesn't override those settings, but both labels stay on the Sensitivity menu.
Allow about 24 hours (24-48 for new groups) before troubleshooting; verify in Word, Excel or PowerPoint, not Outlook, for the Files scope.

units.title: Verify classification is working with Purview reporting
points: Content explorer: current snapshot of items with sensitivity labels, retention labels or matching SITs across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams.
Activity explorer: label applied, changed (upgraded, downgraded, removed) and DLP match events, up to 30 days from the unified audit logs.
Tab access (Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, or Information Protection roles) differs from permission to view item contents.

units.title: Verify classification supports safe Microsoft Copilot grounding
points: Copilot only respects existing protection: VIEW to open encrypted content, plus EXTRACT to use it in a response.
It displays and inherits the highest-priority label by label rank (least restrictive at top of list), not by policy order.
DKE-protected content isn't accessible to Copilot or agents.
Gaps: Teams meeting and channel chat labels aren't recognized (invites and calendar events are fine); container labels aren't inherited by items.

keyTerms.definition: Pattern-based detector using regex, keywords, proximity and checksum to produce a confidence level.
Classification against a securely hashed table of known values, narrowing matches to those values.
Machine-learning classifier trained on examples to recognize free-form content.
Item scope protects files, emails and meetings; Groups & sites scope protects the Microsoft 365 group, team or site.
Order that decides which policy's settings win when several apply to a user.
Encryption whose content Copilot and agents can't access.
Right Copilot needs, in addition to VIEW, to use encrypted content in a response.

tables.title: Choosing a classification technique
rows: A predictable shape (regex, keywords, proximity, checksum)
Consistently formatted data such as a transaction reference
Values present in a hashed reference table
A known, fixed list such as an account roster
Free-form, varied content such as case files

tables.title: Two priority orders
rows: Which policy's settings win for a user
Label ranking for downgrade detection and auto-labeling match resolution; also Copilot label inheritance (rank)

remember: Fixed list of known values → think **EDM**; free-form prose → **trainable classifier**; predictable format → **SIT**.
Container label (Groups & sites) → protects the **space**, not the files inside it, and isn't inherited by items in Copilot.
Overlapping policies → **union of labels**, but **settings come from the one highest-priority policy**.
Copilot and encrypted content → **VIEW is not enough**, it also needs EXTRACT; DKE is never available.

selfCheck.q: Which technique reduces matches against invented numbers that look like valid account numbers from a known roster?
selfCheck.a: Exact data match against a hashed reference table.

selfCheck.q: Policy A requires downgrade justification; higher-priority Policy B doesn't. A user is in both. What happens?
selfCheck.a: Policy B's setting applies, so no justification is required; settings don't merge. The user still sees labels from both policies.

selfCheck.q: A user can open an encrypted file but Copilot can't use it in a response. Why might that be?
selfCheck.a: The label's usage rights include VIEW but not EXTRACT, which Copilot also needs (or the file uses DKE, which Copilot can't access).

modules.title: Prevent data loss and govern the data lifecycle with Microsoft Purview
modules.learnSummary: Specify data loss prevention requirements across Microsoft 365 workloads and Microsoft Copilot, respond to DLP alerts, specify data lifecycle management requirements, and monitor AI activity using Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI.
modules.tldr: DLP requirements always name a location, a condition and an action, and Copilot and Agent 365 are covered by separate controls. You respond to alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR or Purview, specify retention with policies, labels and label policies, and use DSPM to monitor AI activity and SharePoint oversharing.
objectives: Identify requirements for DLP policies across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, endpoints, and Microsoft Copilot.
Review and respond to DLP alerts, including alerts correlated in Microsoft Defender.
Identify requirements for data lifecycle management, including retention labels, retention label policies, and retention policies.
Monitor and secure AI activity by using Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI.
Recognize the broader Microsoft Purview governance surface, including reporting and alerting, insider risk management, and auditing.
keyPoints: Every DLP requirement = **location + condition + action**. Endpoints (Windows 10/11 and recent macOS) need **device onboarding** to Purview first.

The **Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat** location is **Custom template only** and disables all other locations in that policy; use a separate policy for Exchange. It doesn't support administrative units; updates can take up to 4 hours.
Prompt-SIT blocking evaluates **only text typed in the prompt**, not uploaded file contents; **simulation mode logs but never blocks**. Sensitivity labels and SITs can't be combined in one rule.

A DLP alert needs **scope, detection type and workload/activity** to line up; a matching SIT alone isn't enough. Copilot policies don't cover Agent 365 interactions, which are scoped by agent instance.

Alert, incident, classification/status/tag and **remediation** are different things; setting an incident to Resolved doesn't fix the user, file or device. Defender incident history is six months; Purview DLP alerts dashboard 30 days.

**Retention policy** = container default; **retention label** = item exception; **retention label policy** = publish (manual) or auto-apply. Retain beats delete, the **longest retain** sets the floor, and a label's delete action takes precedence over policy delete actions.
**Preservation Lock** is irreversible, blocks even Global Administrators from relaxing the policy, doesn't support adaptive scopes, and label policies must contain only regulatory-record labels.
Current **DSPM**: AI observability (what exists), Activity explorer (what happened), data risk assessments (where oversharing sits). Also recognize Insider Risk Management and Purview Audit.

units.title: Specify DLP requirements across Microsoft 365 locations
points: Exchange: outbound mail; SharePoint/OneDrive: block guest access while internal access continues; Teams: chat and channel messages; Endpoints: device activities such as USB copy.
Copilot conditions/actions: sensitivity label, SIT in prompts, SIT in web search, external email; action Prevent Copilot from processing content (prompts action in preview).
Label action stops Copilot using the content but the item may still appear in citations; external email is excluded from grounding (only sender metadata evaluated).
Microsoft Agent 365 DLP uses separate workload-bound controls.

units.title: Exercise - Create a DLP policy for Microsoft Copilot
points: Data loss prevention > Policies > Custom policy; keep Full directory and select the Copilot location, scoped to a pilot group.
Rule: content contains a SIT, action Restrict/Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts, Block.
Run in simulation mode first, then switch to On; allow up to four hours each time.
Needs E5 or E5 Compliance licensing and a role such as Purview Data Security AI Admin or Compliance Administrator.

units.title: Attribute DLP alerts across AI apps and agents
points: Read an alert as scope, detection type and workload/activity; policy mode and alert configuration must also align.
Agent 365: an agent instance is scoped like a user (directly or via a security group); supported interactions are agent-to-human and human-to-agent in Teams, OneDrive/SharePoint and email.
The Copilot prompt policy doesn't evaluate an Agent 365 interaction; only an Agent 365 policy can.

units.title: Respond to DLP alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR
points: Defender XDR unified incident queue gives cross-solution context; Purview DLP alerts dashboard and Activity explorer give DLP-specific detail.
Filter Incidents & alerts > Incidents by service source Microsoft Data Loss Prevention; tags document handling only.
In-place remediation on users, files and devices (e.g. apply retention label, remove risky share, disable account); some actions need another console.
Advanced Hunting can combine compliance and security signals.

units.title: Exercise - Review a DLP alert in Microsoft Defender XDR
points: Read Alert story and Sensitive info types tabs: policy, rule, user, file, workload, SIT, severity.
Choose proportionate remediation; use Go hunt when more context is needed.
Keep status In progress until work is complete; classification and status are documentation only.
Defender XDR alert-tuning rule reclassifies DLP signals as behaviors from early October 2026; check Alert tuning if alerts stop appearing.

units.title: Specify data lifecycle management requirements
points: Example: three-year site retention policy plus a seven-year retention label for regulated case records; auto-apply can use a SIT, keyword or trainable classifier.

Principles: retention wins over deletion; longest retain action is the floor; label delete action takes precedence over policy deletes; adaptive or specific-instance scopes beat organization-wide scopes before shortest delete period.
A disposition review only occurs when a label is configured to start one; physical deletion can lag (timer jobs, Recycle Bin).
Preservation Lock needs validation by records, legal and compliance owners before applying.

units.title: Monitor AI activity and oversharing risk with Data Security Posture Management
points: AI observability inventories observed apps and agents (including Agent 365); start there for an unfamiliar agent.
Activity explorer: Copilot experiences and agents, Enterprise AI apps, Other AI apps; viewing prompts and responses needs an extra content-viewer permission.
Data risk assessments: default Microsoft 365 assessment runs weekly on the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage (first results up to four days); custom ones need at least 48 hours and don't refresh.
Third-party AI coverage depends on the integration; don't confuse current DSPM with DSPM for AI (classic).

units.title: Exercise - Review a data risk assessment in Data Security Posture Management
points: Open DSPM > Discover > Data risk assessments; note default vs. custom, scope, status and last run.
Compare access (users, groups, Anyone or organization-wide links) with who actually needs it.
Next actions: tighten sharing, apply a sensitivity label, or escalate to the site owner.

units.title: Recognize the broader Microsoft Purview governance surface
points: Reporting and alerting: Information Protection, DLP and custom posture reports (in preview) show trends, not proof of control effectiveness.

Insider Risk Management correlates behavior patterns, pseudonymizes users by default, and has Risky AI usage and agent (Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry) templates; custom policies are specialist work.
Purview Audit gives searchable, retained records of user and admin operations, including supported Copilot and AI activity; it supports, not proves, an investigation.

keyTerms.definition: The three-part model every DLP requirement must name.
Container-level retention applied to a location such as all of SharePoint or a site.
Item-level retention used as the exception to a container default.
Publishes a retention label for manual use or auto-applies it based on a SIT, keyword or trainable classifier.
Irreversible lock preventing anyone from disabling or weakening a retention policy.
Scan of SharePoint sites for oversharing, over-permissioned or newly exposed content.
Purview solution correlating user and agent signals to surface insider risk, pseudonymized by default.

tables.title: Where to look for which DSPM question
rows: What AI apps and agents exist and how risky are they?
Activity explorer (extra permission for prompt/response content)
Is a risky behavior pattern building?

tables.title: Purview DLP alerts vs. Defender XDR incidents
headers: Purview DLP alerts dashboard / Activity explorer

remember: Copilot location chosen in a policy → **all other locations are disabled**; use a second policy for Exchange.
Container default vs. item exception → **retention policy vs. retention label**; the longest retain action wins over a shorter delete.
Marking an incident Resolved → **not remediation**.
Unfamiliar agent in the logs → **AI observability**; SharePoint oversharing → **data risk assessment**; who-did-what → **Audit**.

selfCheck.q: Relecloud wants to block sensitive text in Copilot prompts and keep Exchange DLP. What design?
selfCheck.a: A custom Copilot-only policy plus a separate Exchange DLP policy, because the Copilot location disables all other locations in its policy.

selfCheck.q: A document has a five-year retain-then-delete policy and a three-year retain-then-delete label. What happens at year three?
selfCheck.a: The label's delete action becomes due but permanent deletion waits until the five-year retain action ends.

selfCheck.q: A Copilot prompt policy in simulation mode matched a prompt. Was the prompt blocked?
selfCheck.a: No. Simulation only records the match; blocking needs enforcement mode and the preview action enabled, plus time to reach Copilot.

paths.title: Manage and secure Microsoft 365 AI services
paths.summary: Roll out, secure, and monitor Microsoft Copilot and agents across a growing tenant—enable Copilot safely, establish and govern agent identities, curate the agent catalog, monitor and govern agents in production, and keep AI services cost-effective and healthy.

modules.title: Assess readiness and roll out Microsoft Copilot
modules.learnSummary: Assess tenant and data readiness for Microsoft Copilot—including the Copilot Readiness Report and update channels—identify and address oversharing and compliance risks, and plan a phased rollout across your organization.
modules.tldr: Before rolling out Microsoft Copilot you check two separate things: tenant readiness (licenses, update channel, app activity) and data readiness (do existing permissions match the intended audience?). You then expand in phases — pilot, validate, expand — and only move on when named evidence passes a go/no-go gate.
objectives: Assess tenant readiness for a Microsoft Copilot rollout, including the Copilot Readiness Report and update channels.
Identify and address data readiness issues—data leaks, oversharing, and compliance gaps—before a rollout.
Plan a phased rollout of Microsoft Copilot across the organization.
keyPoints: The **Copilot readiness report** (Reports > Usage > Copilot > Readiness tab) covers 28 days, can lag up to 72 hours, and shows license, update-channel and app-activity values — **no composite 'ready' status**.

Microsoft 365 Apps needs **Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel** for Copilot. Treat **Uses eligible update channel** as the authoritative value; if it is No, check config.office.com > Inventory.
**Suggested candidate for Copilot** = top 25% of unlicensed users by app usage, re-evaluated weekly. It is a prioritization signal, not an employee ranking or access control.
Copilot **respects existing permissions** and never grants new access, but it makes authorized content easier to **discover**. Oversharing (for example an EEEU grant) becomes visible after rollout.
Use **separate evidence sources** (site permissions snapshot, EEEU activity report, Content Management Assessment, DSPM data risk assessment) — each has its own population, freshness and limits.

Handle risk in three steps: **identify, protect on an interim basis, remediate**. RCD hides a site from org-wide search and Copilot discovery; RAC denies users outside control groups; neither replaces removing the broad grant.
Rollout runs **pilot, validate, expand**. A clean pilot proves only what it tested; expansion needs named evidence and measurable thresholds, and a failed or missing check is a **no-go (hold)**.
Assigning a Copilot license changes **availability, not SharePoint permissions**.

units.title: Assess tenant readiness for a Microsoft Copilot rollout
points: Report location: Reports > Usage > Copilot > Copilot > Readiness. Four summary charts: Total Prerequisite Licenses, Users on an eligible update channel, Assigned Licenses, Available Licenses.

Roles that can open it include AI Administrator, Global Administrator, Reports Reader and others; Usage Summary Reports Reader sees it without user details. A License Administrator or User Administrator assigns seats.
Activity columns (Teams meetings/chat, Outlook email, Office docs) are adoption signals, not access controls.
Wider checklist: test environment, pilot, communication plan, Conditional Access review, SharePoint governance and data readiness review, network validation.

units.title: Exercise - Run and interpret the Microsoft Copilot readiness report
points: Readiness is not available in GCC, GCC High, DoD or Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.
Separate technical conditions (license, channel) from adoption signals (activity) when deciding on a row.
Assigning a license does not change a device's update channel; browser-based access and desktop-app readiness are different checks.
The export is not a complete entitlement inventory and does not prove SharePoint authorization is appropriate.

units.title: Identify and resolve data readiness issues
points: Data leaks, oversharing and compliance gaps concern both permission (can open) and discoverability (can find).

Evidence sources: Site permissions snapshot (baseline, CSV up to 1 million sites, run at most every 30 days), EEEU activity report (top 100 sites, last 28 days), Content Management Assessment, DSPM data risk assessment (weekly default, top 100 sites).

Controls: RCD (temporary, discovery only, no OneDrive), DLP (name the exact condition and action), site access review (workflow, not proof), RAC (needs normal permission plus control-group membership, up to 10 groups per site).
Disabling EEEU for future selection does not remove existing grants; remove them explicitly and test. Purview Audit is monitoring, not remediation.

units.title: Exercise - Remediate an oversharing risk before rollout
points: Find the exposure in SharePoint admin center > Reports > Site permissions for your organization; EEEU is potential exposure, not proof of access.
Remove the EEEU grant (keeps the intended Finance group) or constrain with RAC (Active sites > Settings > Restricted site access).
Confirm with Check Permissions for an allowed and a non-member user; another grant or an item-specific exception can still give access.
A new snapshot can take up to 24 hours (first one up to five days); a pending report does not mean the change failed.

units.title: Plan a phased rollout across the organization
points: Course model: Pilot, Validate, Expand. Microsoft's setup guidance names its phases Pilot, Deploy, Operate.
Validate gate needs timestamped readiness evidence, approved scope, control evidence, access tests (allowed and denied user), discovery evidence, fresh reports and decision evidence with thresholds.
Positive sentiment alone does not pass the gate; if a check fails or is missing, hold at the current population and return to validate.
Stale or missing evidence can justify an honest 'wait' decision.

units.title: Exercise - Stage a phased pilot rollout group
points: Create a new security group (for example Copilot Pilot - Wave 1) with Assigned membership, and do not reuse a group that grants app access or other licenses.
Assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot license to the group (Billing > Licenses); group licensing uses seats already purchased and shows problems on the Errors & issues tab.
A group assignment does not replace or double-count a user's direct assignment.
Usage reports lag about two days, so licensing success is not adoption.

keyTerms.definition: Microsoft 365 admin center report showing licenses, update-channel eligibility and app activity for the past 28 days.
Everyone except external users — a broad grant covering current and future internal users, a common oversharing source.
Temporary site-level control that removes a SharePoint site from org-wide search and Copilot discovery without changing permissions.
Denies users outside configured control groups, even with earlier permissions; allowed users still need normal permission.
Source of site permission, EEEU and assessment reports; needs an eligible base subscription plus a Copilot license, SAM Plan 1 or E7.
Measurable criterion that must be met before the rollout expands to the next group.

tables.title: Evidence sources for data readiness
rows: Site permissions for your organization snapshot
Permissions, groups, EEEU, sharing links, owner, sensitivity; web view top 100 sites, CSV up to 1 million
First run up to 5 days, later up to 24 hours, data up to 48 hours old; run at most every 30 days; current permission baseline
Top 100 sites by items or groups shared with EEEU in the past 28 days
Up to 24 hours; activity, not the current EEEU baseline
Inactive sites, ownership, broken inheritance, EEEU, permissive links
2 to 72 hours; no action without admin consent; every 30 days
Top 100 SharePoint sites by usage, adds sensitivity context
Weekly default, first results after 4 days; custom results need 48 hours and must be rerun after changes

remember: Copilot exposes oversharing, it doesn't create it → fix the **permission** (remove EEEU grant), don't blame the license.
RCD → **discovery** only; RAC → **access** (needs normal permission AND control-group membership). Neither changes the other.
A successful pilot or an empty report → **not proof**; stale data means wait, not pass.

selfCheck.q: The readiness report shows a user as a suggested candidate but 'Uses eligible update channel' is No. What does that tell you and what do you do?
selfCheck.a: The user is a high-usage unlicensed candidate, but desktop apps are not on an eligible channel; corroborate in config.office.com > Inventory. A license alone does not fix the channel.

selfCheck.q: An admin disables future selection of EEEU, but an existing site still grants it. What must be done?
selfCheck.a: Explicitly remove the existing grant (or constrain with RAC) and then verify access with a direct test.

selfCheck.q: Half-way through a wave a go/no-go threshold fails. What happens?
selfCheck.a: It is a no-go: stop assigning licenses to the next group, hold at the current population and return to validate until the gap is closed.

modules.title: Configure Microsoft Copilot settings and extensibility
modules.learnSummary: Configure the Microsoft Copilot tenant-settings catalog, manage web search and Cowork administration, set up Copilot Search, and extend Copilot with Copilot Connectors and third-party AI providers.
modules.tldr: This module covers where Microsoft Copilot is governed: the settings catalog, web search (Cloud Policy), Cowork access, Copilot Search, third-party AI providers and Copilot connectors. For each control, ask who is affected, how fast, and which admin surface and role apply.
objectives: Configure the Microsoft Copilot tenant-settings catalog and identify each setting's admin-center location.
Manage web search for Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat, and configure Copilot Search.
Govern Cowork access and web-search behavior without authorizing chargeable usage.
Manage third-party AI providers and evaluate whether a provider offering is handled as a Microsoft subprocessor or an independent processor.
Configure Copilot Connectors and choose connector types that balance richer grounding against expanded data exposure.
Recognize awareness-level extensibility surfaces, including SharePoint AI skills and the Copilot Frontier program.
keyPoints: The **settings catalog** is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings. AI Administrator changes it, Global Reader views it; release preferences also accept Office Apps Administrator or Security Administrator.

**Release audiences**: Standard (default GA), Deferred (deferred-capable updates 30 days after Standard), Frontier (pre-GA, managed separately). Group exceptions use an Entra security group, limit 100 users, up to 24 hours.

**Web search** is one Cloud Policy setting, **Allow web search in Copilot**, configured in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. The policy is the ceiling; users can only turn it off, never beyond the policy.
**Cowork access** needs a Copilot license, an enabled environment and a **spending policy** that selects Cowork. The old Agents > All Agents > Cowork surface has no effect on access.
**Copilot Search** needs no setup: eligible Copilot-licensed users get it, others get Microsoft Search. Admins add acronyms (Published, up to a day) and bookmarks (title, URL, keywords).

**Independent processors** (Mistral, SpaceXAI independent offering, Anthropic with Data Retention) fall outside Microsoft DPA safeguards; **subprocessors** (Anthropic, OpenAI-operated) fall under Microsoft terms. Assignments are provider-level and take hours.

**Connector types**: tenant-configured synced and self-serve synced index content; **federated** connectors fetch live via MCP, with the source checking permissions at query time. 'No indexing' does not mean no data transfer.
**SharePoint AI skills** have no on/off switch; govern via site permissions, retention, labels and auditing. **Frontier** is a tenant-level opt-in decision requiring a Copilot license.

units.title: Configure the Microsoft Copilot tenant-settings catalog
points: Catalog controls: self-service purchases (Allow, Allow trials only, Do not allow), Copilot in admin centers, image generation, AI Disclaimer, release preferences.
Image generation set to Don't allow: PowerPoint can still use stock or brand images; Copilot Chat returns no substitute image.
AI Disclaimer (Standard or Bold, optional policy URL) shows in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote and the Copilot app, not in SharePoint, OneDrive, Whiteboard or Forms.
Modern Standard/Deferred options are not available in GCC, GCC High or DoD; those use Targeted and Standard.

units.title: Exercise - Configure the Microsoft Copilot settings catalog
points: Set Deferred release for the organization and assign the pilot Entra security group to Standard release so pilot users get GA features first.
Release preference changes can take up to 24 hours; neither this setting nor image generation governs Frontier access.
Image generation: Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot image generation (or under Copilot actions).

units.title: Manage web search for Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat
points: Three policy states: enabled in both, disabled in both, disabled in Work mode only (which also disables web search in Researcher and Cowork).
Office Apps Administrator is recommended; Security Administrator and Global Administrator also work. Scope can be all users or selected groups; not supported in 21Vianet.
Assigned groups usually get Cloud Policy changes within 90 minutes; others check again in 24 hours; applies next time the Office app opens.
Generated Bing queries have user and tenant identifiers removed, and the DPA, HIPAA and EU Data Boundary do not apply to them. A missing citation does not prove the policy failed.

units.title: Manage Copilot Cowork
points: Access needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, an environment where Cowork is enabled, and usage-based billing granted through a spending policy that selects Cowork.
A spending policy is an access control, not just a budget; to keep a user out, leave them out of every spending policy that selects Cowork. Enabling one can authorize chargeable usage.
Cowork web search follows the Cloud Policy state only, with no user toggle: choose Enabled with the option Disabled in Work mode, Enabled in Web mode and Chat.
Cloud Policy applies to user objects, so scope the pilot to user accounts, not a device-only group. Not supported in 21Vianet, GCC, GCC High or DoD.

units.title: Configure Copilot Search
points: Searches Microsoft 365 content and configured third-party connector sources; public web search is a separate feature.
Configured at Copilot > Search; a Search Administrator adds acronym answers. Existing Microsoft Search acronyms and bookmarks need no extra enablement.
Draft acronyms do not appear; Published ones can take up to one day. Bookmarks refresh the index immediately, but ranking varies by user.
Verify entries as a licensed user with patterns like 'define', 'meaning of', 'stands for'.

units.title: Exercise - Configure web search and Copilot Search
points: Cloud Policy path: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management, scoped to the pilot group.
If behavior differs, check propagation time and whether a higher-priority Cloud Policy configuration overrides it.
Acronyms are added at Copilot > Search > Acronyms with state Published; allow up to one day and test as a licensed user.

units.title: Manage third-party AI providers
points: AI subprocessor = handled for Microsoft under the DPA and Product Terms; AI independent processor = own terms, outside Microsoft safeguards. Role and geography are not implied by the legal class.
SpaceXAI as independent processor requires Global Administrator; Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI-operated and Anthropic with Data Retention accept AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
Assignments are provider-level (not model-level), support users, security groups or nested groups, up to 999 combined assignments, enforced across Copilot, Copilot Studio and Power Platform.
Accepting independent-processor terms is a legal commitment; roll back with No users and verify with a previously allowed user after the propagation window (hours).

units.title: Exercise - Enable a third-party AI provider
points: Mistral and SpaceXAI: Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers for other large language models. Anthropic and OpenAI: AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
Pilot users need an eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot license; if the provider card is not available for the tenant or cloud, that is a valid result.
Assign a selected group, wait a few hours, verify in a surface showing provider or model choice, and check for broader assignments.

units.title: Configure Copilot connectors
points: Deployment needs the AI Administrator role; Copilot grounding needs a Copilot add-on or Microsoft 365 E7, and every user querying a federated source needs that license.

Synced connector: Copilot > Connectors > Gallery; choose Only users with access to the content, verify identity mapping, run a full crawl after ACL changes (incremental crawls skip permission changes).
Federated: users authenticate via OAuth, the source enforces permissions at query time, Purview auditability still applies; Work IQ custom tooling is preview and not for production.
Remove: turn Copilot Visibility off (up to 30 minutes), or delete the connection and avoid the Delete failed state.

units.title: Govern SharePoint AI skills and the Frontier program
points: SharePoint skills (preview) are reusable multi-step tasks saved as Markdown in the Agent Assets library on each site; Edit permission creates, View permission runs, and a skill never expands what the user can already do.
No single on/off switch: existing site permissions, retention, labels and auditing are the controls, so get them right before users build skills.
Frontier gives early access to emerging agents and experiences before GA; tenant-level opt-in, with control over which users get which capabilities; requires a Copilot license.

keyTerms.definition: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center service that applies settings (such as Allow web search in Copilot) to user objects, scoped to all users or groups.
Access control that selects Cowork and enables usage-based billing for users in scope.
Provider that handles data for Microsoft under the Microsoft DPA, Product Terms and enterprise safeguards.
Provider that handles data under its own terms, outside Microsoft safeguards.
Connector that fetches live results through MCP without indexing or storing source data in Microsoft 365.
Program for early, pre-GA access to Copilot agents and AI experiences, managed at tenant level.

tables.title: Which connector model?
rows: Indexes content, metadata and ACL in Microsoft 365
Indexes content the individual user selects
Live fetch via MCP; no index or storage in Microsoft 365
Admin enables; user authenticates and consents
Admin enables; user authenticates; source enforces permissions

tables.title: Release audiences
rows: Pre-GA, subject to change, not under GA SLAs
Frontier controls, not the GA setting

remember: Web search policy lives in the **Microsoft 365 Apps admin center (Cloud Policy)**, not the Copilot settings page — the page only links to it.
Cowork access → **spending policy**, not the legacy Agents > All Agents entry.
SpaceXAI independent processor → **Global Administrator only**; most other providers accept AI Administrator too.
ACL changed on a synced connector → run a **full crawl**; incremental crawls won't pick it up.

selfCheck.q: Users complain web search stopped in Copilot Work mode but works in Web mode and Chat. Which policy state is configured, and what else does it affect?
selfCheck.a: Allow web search in Copilot is set to disabled in Work mode only; this also disables web search in Researcher and Cowork.

selfCheck.q: An admin sets a provider to No users and immediately tests with a previously allowed user, who still gets in. Has the rollback failed?
selfCheck.a: Not necessarily; provider changes take hours to propagate, so verify after the propagation window.

selfCheck.q: Which connector model keeps source data out of a Microsoft 365 index and has the source check permissions at query time?
selfCheck.a: A federated connector (via MCP), though requested data is still transferred at runtime.

modules.title: Establish agent identities and secure access with Microsoft Entra Agent ID
modules.learnSummary: Establish governed identities for AI agents using Microsoft Entra Agent ID—assign sponsors and Microsoft Entra owners, automate sponsor-transfer lifecycle transitions, and apply Conditional Access to secure agent access.
modules.tldr: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives AI agents a purpose-built identity model with a blueprint, an agent identity and an optional user account. Sponsors provide business accountability, owners provide technical administration, Lifecycle Workflows keep sponsorship current, and Conditional Access (scoped to the blueprint principal) controls token requests.
objectives: Explain the Microsoft Entra Agent ID identity model, including agent identity blueprints, agent identities, and agent user accounts.
Assign sponsors and Microsoft Entra owners to an agent identity, distinct from Agent Registry ownership.
Automate sponsor-transfer lifecycle transitions using Microsoft Entra ID Governance Lifecycle Workflows.
Apply Conditional Access to agent identities and select the correct licensing model.
keyPoints: A plain service principal has no enforced **sponsorship**, no agent-aware audit and no blueprint lifecycle. Agent ID adds blueprint, blueprint principal, agent identity and optional agent user account.

The **blueprint holds the credentials** (federated credentials, certificates or keys, client secrets); child agent identities store none, and the agent identity is the acting client in tokens and logs.
An **agent user account** is optional, 1:1 with an agent identity, and needed only when a system strictly requires a user object (shared mailbox, Teams channel, document library).
There is **no in-place conversion** of an app registration or service principal; migrate side by side, with at least one sponsor required at creation.

**Sponsor** = business accountability (can disable, edit sponsors, soft-delete). **Owner** = technical administration (credentials, restore, hard-delete). The **Agent Registry owner** is a third, separate relationship in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Only the task **Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager** changes sponsorship, in a Mover or Leaver workflow, and the sponsor needs a populated manager attribute. It does not change the Entra owner or Registry owner.
Conditional Access on an agent identity covers only that identity; select the **blueprint principal** to cover current and future children. It does not cover the agent's user account.

For an agent identity, **Block access** is the only control and **Agent risk (Preview)** the only condition. Use **Report-only** first; baseline needs Microsoft 365 E7 or Agent 365 plus Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.

units.title: Understand the Microsoft Entra Agent ID object model
points: Four objects: agent identity blueprint (template and credential holder), blueprint principal (tenant presence, audit object), agent identity (single-tenant service principal with agent subtype), agent's user account (optional).
Interactive agents use OAuth on-behalf-of (agent identity is subject, user in the actor claim); autonomous agents use client credentials under their own identity.

Creation channels include Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Teams Developer Portal, Microsoft Agent 365, Azure App Service or Functions, and third-party agents via the Entra Auth SDK or workload identity federation.
New objects can have read-after-write delay: wait 30 to 60 seconds with exponential backoff.

units.title: Assign a sponsor and a Microsoft Entra owner
points: Sponsors for agent identities, blueprints and blueprint principals: users (including guests) and groups with dynamic membership or Microsoft 365 groups; role-assignable groups are not supported. Agent user accounts accept any group.
Owners can be users, guests or service principals, never groups; ownership applies to the assigned object only.
A sponsor can't edit authentication settings, manage credentials, re-enable, restore or hard-delete.
Sponsorship does not transfer automatically when the sponsor leaves, and Registry owner reassignment is separate.

units.title: Exercise - Assign a sponsor and owner to an agent identity
points: Needs Agent ID Administrator or being an owner. Path: Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities > Access > Owners and sponsors.
Sponsorship is additive: adding a co-sponsor does not replace the first sponsor; keep at least one.
Agent identity ownership does not make someone owner of its blueprint; compare with the Registry owner in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

units.title: Automate sponsor transfer with Lifecycle Workflows
points: Three sponsor tasks, all Mover and Leaver tasks (not Joiner): transfer sponsorships to manager, email the manager, email co-sponsors. Only the transfer task changes sponsorship.
Transfer task: gets the manager, finds each sponsored agent identity, adds the manager as sponsor, removes the employee.
History status: continueOnError true gives Completed with errors; false gives Failed. No automatic retry or rollback.
Least-privileged role is Lifecycle Workflows Administrator; licensing is Microsoft 365 E7, or Agent 365 plus Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.

units.title: Exercise - Configure a sponsor-transfer Lifecycle Workflow
points: Use the Pre-Offboarding of an employee template, keep the time-based trigger on employeeLeaveDateTime, and replace default tasks with the sponsor tasks.
The What-if tool previews scope and failures without performing tasks, supports only time-based triggers, and needs an ID Governance or Entra Suite license.
Run on demand to test; after a run, confirm sponsorship on Owners and sponsors and that the technical owner is unchanged.
An overall failure does not undo tasks that already succeeded.

units.title: Apply Conditional Access to agent identities and choose the right license
points: Policy on one agent identity covers only it; the blueprint principal in the agent picker covers current and future children, evaluated on fresh token requests.
Agent identity: Block access only, Agent risk (Preview) only condition. Agent user account: endpoint controls such as compliant device. OBO user is evaluated by user-targeted policy.
Not enforced when the blueprint acquires a token to create identities, when Security Defaults are on, or when the agent uses an API key.
Agent risk needs Entra ID P2 during preview; Conditional Access Administrator creates the policy, Reports Reader reads sign-in evidence.

units.title: Exercise - Apply Conditional Access to an agent identity blueprint
points: Create a Block policy under Users, agents (Preview) or workload identities > Agents, pick the blueprint, select the target resource, and leave it in Report-only.
Saved configuration proves only configuration, not evaluation; read results in sign-in logs.
Report-only: Failure = would have blocked; Report-only: Not applied = identity was out of scope (for example excluded). Requests still succeed in report-only.
Protecting paired agent user accounts needs a second policy.

keyTerms.definition: Template and authentication foundation for agent identities; holds credentials and starts the token exchange.
Runtime identity of a specific agent: a single-tenant service principal with an agent subtype and no credentials of its own.
Optional 1:1 user object paired with an agent identity for systems that require a user.
Human or group accountable for an agent's purpose, lifecycle decisions and access reviews.
Technical administrator of an agent identity, scoped to the assigned object.
Conditional Access state that records the verdict a policy would reach without enforcing it.

tables.title: Sponsor vs owner vs Agent Registry owner
rows: Purpose, lifecycle decisions, access reviews; can disable, edit sponsors, soft-delete
Technical administration: credentials, add relationships, disable, delete, re-enable, restore, hard-delete
Registry metadata and administrative settings in Microsoft 365

remember: Credentials → on the **blueprint**, never on child agent identities.
Sponsor transfer happens only with the **Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager** task; notification tasks transfer nothing, and owners and Registry owners don't change.
Conditional Access on the blueprint principal → covers **agent identities**, not their **user accounts**.
Agent identity can't complete interactive remediation → **Block access only**, no compliant-device control.

selfCheck.q: Engineering will create three more agents from the same blueprint. Where do you scope the Conditional Access policy so they are protected from day one?
selfCheck.a: On the agent identity blueprint principal, which covers current and future child agent identities.

selfCheck.q: A leaver workflow only contains the two email tasks. What happens to the departing sponsor's agent identities?
selfCheck.a: Nothing changes; only the Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager task changes sponsorship, and the sponsor needs a populated manager attribute.

selfCheck.q: An autonomous agent must open a shared mailbox that requires a user object. What identity design fits?
selfCheck.a: Pair the agent identity with an agent user account; both objects exist side by side.

modules.title: Curate and control agents with the Agent Registry and Agent 365 tools
modules.learnSummary: Govern what agents can invoke using Agent 365 tools, including MCP servers, and curate the ongoing agent estate using Registry actions beyond initial onboarding.
modules.tldr: Administrators govern which tools agents can invoke through the Agent Tools registry (Available vs Blocked, plus approval of Bring Your Own MCP servers with separate Entra consent). They also curate the agent estate with ongoing Agent Registry actions and audit it by publisher type and channel.
objectives: Review, approve, and block tools for agents, including Bring Your Own (BYO) MCP server requests.

Manage ongoing Agent Registry actions beyond initial onboarding, including uploading a custom agent, reassigning an already-active agent's owner, deleting an agent, and starting or stopping Microsoft Foundry agents.
Filter and audit the agent estate by publisher type and channel.
keyPoints: The tools registry is at **Agents > Tools > Registry** (Available or Blocked); **Requests** holds pending BYO MCP registrations. AI Administrator is the least-privileged role.
**Approval and Microsoft Entra consent are separate**: approve the request, then grant the exact consent. Client discovery and first invocation (connection, API key) are further steps.

**Block a tool** to remove one capability across supported clients without deleting agents that use it; blocking an agent governs the agent, not its tools. Block and Unblock are separate from Approve and Reject.

BYO MCP (preview) works in Copilot Studio, Visual Studio Code, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI, not Azure AI Foundry or Declarative Agents. Delete and republish are unsupported, so **block** retires a server.

Review requests as **Accept** (proportionate permissions, complete evidence), **Reject** (excessive or unrelated permission) or **Conditional** (evidence missing; a review class, not an admin-center status).

**Assign new owner** fully replaces the owner (previous owner loses all access) for Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents; deleting is documented for Agent Builder agents, is irreversible and takes up to 24 hours.
Starting or stopping a **Foundry agent** provisions or deallocates compute and needs **Azure AI Owner**; AI Administrator does not grant it.
Registry filters give a **candidate inventory** (Publisher Type, Channel, Status), not proof a person can use an agent; validate Users, Permissions, license and connection.

units.title: Review, approve, and block tools for agents
points: Registry lists name, status, type and publisher; Available does not prove review history, authorization, data access or actual use.

BYO flow: developer registers (pending request), AI Administrator or Global Administrator approves or rejects, administrator grants Entra consent, supported client discovers it, user needs audience, license, permissions and data access.
Copilot Studio discovery can take up to 30 minutes after approval and consent; no published timing for other clients, and no published block propagation SLA.
Blocking SharePoint or Foundry agents affects only Microsoft Copilot Chat; blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other hosts.

units.title: Exercise - Review requests and control tool availability
points: Check that the requested scope matches the declared tools: read-only tools with Cases.Read.All, clear ownership, authentication and data boundary is an Accept; consent is still a separate step.
Block then Unblock a tool in Registry; the tool shows Blocked or Available again, and changes can take a few minutes to reach clients.
Blocking a tool doesn't delete agents, revoke other permissions or undo consent.

units.title: Govern bring your own MCP servers
points: Registration needs Agent 365 CLI 1.1.165-preview or later, the provisioned Agent 365 service principal, and a public remote HTTPS endpoint; developer runs a365 develop-mcp register-external-mcp-server.
Authentication types: NoAuth, APIKey (header or query), ExternalOAuth, EntraOAuth.
Reviewer verifies declared tools, exact scopes, endpoint ownership, authentication, data boundaries, retention, geography and third-party security.
Defender advanced hunting can observe ExecuteToolByGateway events with the right permissions and license; gateway telemetry does not mean Microsoft endorsement.

units.title: Exercise - Review a bring your own model context protocol (MCP) server registration
points: Request asking Knowledge.ReadWrite.All plus Directory.ReadWrite.All for a read-only lookup: Reject and ask for Knowledge.Read.All and no directory permission.
Request missing owner attestation, rotation owner for the API key and data boundary: Conditional; send it back rather than approve.
After approval, grant consent, check Registry shows Available, then connect from a client; first use can still need setup such as an API key.
Retire with Block; this isn't revocation of the external API key.

units.title: Perform ongoing Agent Registry curation
points: Upload a custom agent: AI Administrator or Global Administrator uploads a ZIP from Agent Builder or Copilot Studio at Agents > All agents > Add agent, then sets Publish and Deploy audiences.

Assign new owner: new owner must be an organization user, gets edit and delete plus the previous owner's files; the previous owner loses all access. Not supported for Foundry, SharePoint or other platforms.
Agent Builder Add owner and Remove owner support multi-owner continuity, unlike Assign new owner.
Deletion removes files and the SharePoint Embedded container; don't generalize it to every agent or use it as routine rollback.

units.title: Exercise - Reassign an active agent's owner
points: Agents > All agents > select agent > Assign new owner > choose person > Assign; selecting a name alone transfers nothing.
For an Agent Builder agent the new owner needs a Microsoft Copilot license; ownerless agents are supported and a departed owner's account needn't stay active.
There is no shared state: the previous owner loses edit, delete and file access immediately, so it isn't the same as adding a delegate.

units.title: Audit the agent estate by publisher and channel
points: Summary numbers: Total agents, Agents without owners, Unmanaged agents (created or managed outside Agent 365); an agent can have an owner and still be unmanaged.
Candidate inventory filters: Publisher Type non-Microsoft, Channel Teams, Status Available.
To confirm a person can use an agent, check Details, Users (Available to, Installed for), Permissions and consent, license and connection, and recent activity.
Security tab and Risks column need Microsoft E7 or Agent 365; Export filtered agents is a point-in-time snapshot with 30+ fields.

keyTerms.definition: Remote MCP server registered by a developer through Agent 365 and governed by an approval and consent flow (preview).
Agents > Tools > Registry list of tools with Available or Blocked status.
Registry action that fully replaces an agent's owner; the previous owner loses all access.
Registry filters: who owns or distributes the agent, and where it is deployed and discoverable.
Agents created or managed outside Agent 365.

tables.title: Ongoing Registry actions
rows: Owner-supplied ZIP from Agent Builder or Copilot Studio
Ownerless or active shared Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agent
Documented for Agent Builder; irreversible, up to 24 hours
Start or stop a Foundry agent

remember: Approve a BYO server → **not enough**; Microsoft Entra consent is a separate admin step.
Retire a BYO MCP server → **Block**, since delete and republish are unsupported.
Tool lever ≠ agent lever: blocking a **tool** keeps the agent; blocking an **agent** doesn't touch its tools.
Registry filters give a **candidate list**, not who can actually use the agent.

selfCheck.q: A Vendor Lookup MCP request has no endpoint owner attestation, no key rotation owner and no stated data boundary. How do you classify it?
selfCheck.a: Conditional: don't approve or grant consent until the evidence is complete; return it to the developer or reject it so a complete request can be submitted.

selfCheck.q: A Copilot Studio agent needs an accountable new owner and a Foundry agent must be stopped. Which action and role apply?
selfCheck.a: Assign new owner (AI Administrator or Global Administrator) for the Copilot Studio agent; stop the Foundry agent as an Azure compute action with the Azure AI Owner role.

selfCheck.q: Your manager asks how many non-Microsoft agents the finance team can use in Teams. Is the filtered count the answer?
selfCheck.a: No, the filter (non-Microsoft, Teams, Available) gives only candidates; validate Users scope, permissions and consent, license, and connection for the finance users.

modules.title: Monitor and manage agents with Microsoft Agent 365
modules.learnSummary: Learn how to monitor using real-time visibility into all agents to detect sprawl, understand usage.
modules.tldr: Microsoft Agent 365 gives admins one place in the Microsoft 365 admin center to see every agent in the tenant: the Overview page for trends and top actions, the Registry for the inventory, and the Agent Map for a visual view by platform. Every agent gets a Microsoft Entra Agent ID identity, and you use these views to spot risk, missing owners and exceptions, then act.
objectives: Explore the agents in your organization
Monitor usage, performance and agent effectiveness
Monitor agents using the registry and agent map
View the security risks associated with the agents
keyPoints: **Microsoft Entra Agent ID** gives each agent a unique, persistent identity, distinct from human users and generic app registrations, so agents can be authenticated, authorized, governed and monitored.

Agents built on **Copilot Studio, Agent 365 Builder, Azure AI Foundry or SharePoint** are registered automatically; agents from **Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI** can be registered in the Agent Registry.
The **Overview** page (Agents > Overview) is the control plane: totals, active users, agent run time, connected platforms, **Top actions for you** and agent analytics.
**Active users** = unique users who interacted with at least one agent in the last 30 days; **agent run time** = total agent-assisted hours in the last 30 days.
The **Registry** (Agents > All agents) is the inventory with per-agent tabs; the **Map** clusters agents by platform, status, publisher type, channel or data source and defaults to platform view.
On the registry, watch **agents at risk, agents without owners, unmanaged agents** and connected platforms; exceptions are fixed by assigning an owner, blocking, or deleting the agent.
**Connected platforms** import external agents into the registry for visibility, but the agents stay managed in the external platform; scheduled sync runs every 24 hours (or use Sync now).
Needed: an **Agent 365 license** and the **AI Administrator** role in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

units.title: Introduction to Microsoft Entra Agent ID
points: Microsoft Entra Agent ID extends Entra identity, access protection, governance and compliance to AI agents (non-human identities).
When you create an agent, the Agent 365 Registry registers it and assigns a unique agent identity.

Microsoft-built platforms (Copilot Studio, Agent 365 Builder, Azure AI Foundry, SharePoint) integrate automatically; non-Microsoft platforms such as Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI can register agents to get an identity.

units.title: Monitor and manage agents
points: Three capabilities: Agent 365 Overview, Agent Registry and Agent Map.
Overview covers Microsoft-created agents and agents detected on connected non-Microsoft platforms; Top actions let you approve requests, block risky agents, assign owners and address exceptions.
Agent analytics: agents by creators, top platforms used to build agents, active users over time and trending agents (last 30 days).
Registry counts Microsoft-built, partner-built and custom agents; the Map shows them as clusters by creation platform.
Drill into an agent to see identity, permissions, data access, activity history and applied controls.

units.title: Scenario
points: Fictitious company Zava wants IT to view all agents, monitor and govern them, track adoption and remediate governance gaps.
Personas: Reed Smith (AI Administrator) and Oscar Ward (Global Administrator), who grants Reed the AI Administrator role.

units.title: Exercise – Monitor agents from the overview page
points: Path: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Overview.
Summary tiles: total agents, unique active users (30 days), agent run time (sum of each session's end minus start) and connected platforms.
Top actions: pending requests to approve and activate, agents with security risks, agents pending owner assignment, agents with exceptions or errors.
Prerequisites: Agent 365 license, AI Administrator role, and Microsoft or partner agents deployed in the tenant.

units.title: Exercise - Monitor agents inventory in registry
points: Agents > All agents opens the Registry tab with total agents, agents at risk, agents without owners, unmanaged agents (created outside Agent 365) and connected platforms.
Filters include creators, availability, channel, platform and acquired; per agent you see active users, sessions, exception rate, assisted hours and last updated.
Per-agent tabs: Details, Users, Data & tools (knowledge sources and MCP servers), Security (Purview, Entra ID Protection, Defender policies), Permissions, Activity, Computer Use and Connected agents.
Knowledge sources are the most critical metadata because they determine how data is protected.

units.title: Exercise - Monitor agents using the agent map
points: Agents > All agents > Map tab: clusters by status, publisher type, platform, channel and data source (default: platform).
Risk indicators: orange highlights and red or gray connection lines (red = exception between connected agents, gray = connected to other agents).
Investigate large clusters of agents from unknown publishers; use Activity tab spikes in exceptions as a risk signal, then Security tab, then block.
Retire or quarantine policy violators and approve agents by applying baseline policies.

units.title: Exercise - View agents with exceptions and take action
points: Exceptions can be missing information, security risks or agents that are not required.
Resolve by assigning an owner and platform, blocking an agent with a security risk, or deleting an agent that is not needed.
Start at Agents > Overview > Top actions for you > Agents with exceptions > View details.

units.title: Exercise - Measure agent effectiveness
points: Use the Agent analytics section on the Overview page to review adoption and performance metrics.
Identify who creates most agents, which build platform is most used, active-user trends and the most actively used agents.

units.title: Exercise – Monitor connected platforms
points: Connected platforms securely connect external AI agent environments (Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI) and sync agents into the registry.
Imported agents appear in the admin center but are managed in the external platform.
Add via + Connect a platform: name, platform, region, auto-import choice, credentials, then Verify authentication and Save changes.
Sync now forces a sync; otherwise it runs on the 24-hour schedule.

keyTerms.definition: Identity and security framework that gives AI agents a unique enterprise identity with authentication, permissions, roles and governance.
Central inventory of all agents in the tenant (Microsoft, partner and custom) with per-agent details, risks and owners.
Interactive visual view of registry agents clustered by platform, status, publisher type, channel or data source.
Agents created or managed outside Agent 365, without its risk protection and observability.
Connections to external agent environments (Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI) that sync agents into the registry.
Total hours worked by agents in the last 30 days, summed from session durations.

tables.title: Which Agent 365 view?
rows: Totals, active users, run time, Top actions, agent analytics
Spot trends and decide where to act first
Check owners, risks, metadata and activity per agent
Clusters by platform, status, publisher, channel, data source
See distribution and connections, find risky clusters

remember: Agents built in Copilot Studio, Agent 365 Builder, Foundry or SharePoint → **auto-registered**; Bedrock or Vertex AI → **connect the platform or register** them.
Imported external agents are **visible in Agent 365 but managed in the external platform**.
Active users and run time are **30-day** figures; the platform sync runs **every 24 hours**.

selfCheck.q: You want to see which build platform is used most and which agents gained the most users over the past 30 days. Where do you look?
selfCheck.a: Agents > Overview, in the Agent analytics section (top platforms and trending agents by active users).

selfCheck.q: An agent shows a spike in exceptions and a red line to a connected agent on the Map. What next?
selfCheck.a: Open its Activity and Security tabs to investigate, then block it (or assign an owner or delete it if the exception is missing info or the agent is not required).

selfCheck.q: Your company builds agents in Google Vertex AI. How do they show up in Agent 365?
selfCheck.a: Add Google Vertex AI under Connected platforms (or register the agents) so they sync into the registry; they remain managed in Vertex AI.

modules.title: Govern agents using Agent 365
modules.learnSummary: Learn how to set up policies and permissions to govern and secure agents.
modules.tldr: Agent 365 governance covers the whole agent lifecycle: tenant settings that control who can use and share which agent types, policy templates and access packages for security and permissions, approval of publish and activation requests, owner assignment, blocking, rules and tool control. Purview audit logs provide traceability.
objectives: Understand governance policies
Set up policies, tenant settings, and permissions for the agents
Perform agent lifecycle management tasks such as activate agents in a governed manner, assign owners, block agents, and use rules to govern agent usage
keyPoints: **Agent settings** (Agents > Settings) control allowed agent types (Microsoft, your organization, external publishers), **user access** and **sharing** for all users, no users, or specific users and groups.

**Policy templates** apply Entra, Purview, Defender and SharePoint controls in one step; default templates exist, and **custom templates** can add Conditional Access, access packages and custom security attributes.
**Access packages** in Microsoft Entra govern which resources an agent identity can access, with approvals, time-bound access, reviews and least privilege.
Requests move through **Pending review** (publish), **Pending activation** and **Pending update**; admins **publish to store** to scope the audience and **activate** to let users create instances.
**Blocking** an agent turns off all its instances until you unblock it; **assigning owners** prevents sprawl, and the creator is the default owner.
**Agent management rules** act in bulk: install Microsoft agents, reassign ownerless Agent Builder agents to the manager, block confirmed-compromised agents.
**Tools** (MCP servers and plugins) are controlled in Agents > Tools through Registry and Requests; admins can approve, block or unblock them.
**Microsoft Purview audit** shows who created, changed, published, approved or deleted an agent and what it accessed.

units.title: Govern agents scenarios
points: Zava IT must manage the agent lifecycle, set governance policies up front and use auditing for traceability.

Personas: Oscar Ward (Global Administrator), Reed Smith (AI Administrator) and Hannah Travis (agent maker); the maker role depends on where the agent is built (for example Foundry maker, Copilot Studio maker).

units.title: Exercise – Set up agent settings and access
points: Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types: allow agents built by Microsoft, by your organization, and/or by external publishers.
User access: all users, no users or specific users and groups, enabling a staged rollout by security group; restricted users cannot see or use any agents in the store.
Sharing: controls who can share agents; restricted users can still share with individuals. Only Agent Builder agents can be shared.
Settings apply automatically when an agent is activated or published.

units.title: Security and governance policies
points: Templates bundle predefined policies from Microsoft Entra, Purview, Defender and SharePoint to standardize governance and cut manual configuration.
Custom templates can include Conditional Access, access packages and custom security attributes.
Conditional Access for agents has assignments, target resources, conditions (such as sign-in risk), grant or block controls and a state of On, Off or Report only.

units.title: Exercise – Set up policy template
points: Path: Agents > Settings > Policy template > Add a new policy template.
Policies must already exist in Microsoft Entra to be selectable; custom security attributes need the Attribute Assignment Administrator role.
The AI Administrator can create and apply access packages but lacks privileges for Conditional Access and custom security attributes.
Templates are chosen from a dropdown (custom plus default) when an agent is activated or published.

units.title: Exercise – Set up permissions using access packages
points: Templates apply security and compliance policies; access packages manage the agent's access to SharePoint sites, Teams, apps and APIs.
Access packages support time-bound access, approvals and periodic access reviews.
Configure in the Microsoft Entra admin center: Agents > Agent identities > the agent > Policies & ID Governance > Access packages.

units.title: Exercise – Onboard an agent
points: Agent templates are preconfigured definitions of capabilities, identity and compliance settings; users discover approved templates and onboard agents.
A user requests the agent (for example in Teams > Apps > Agents for your team), admin approval is required, then the user creates and configures it.
Prerequisite: a Microsoft Agent 365 Frontier subscription (25 users) enabled by the tenant admin for autonomous agents.

units.title: Exercise – Deploy and activate agents
points: Requests tab states: Pending review (publish), Pending activation (users can create instances) and Pending update.
Before approving, review the Details, Data & Tools, Security and Permissions tabs (least privilege).
Publish to store: scope to specific users or groups or the whole tenant, choose optional pre-install users, apply a template and review permissions.
Activate: approve the user request (Approve request and activate) and choose who can create instances.

units.title: Exercise - Assign owners to agents to prevent agent sprawl
points: Owners can edit, publish and manage settings of the agent; the creator is the default owner.
Reassignment of shared agents is supported only for Agent Builder and Copilot Studio agents.
Use Top actions > Assign owners, or All agents with the Agents without owners filter.

units.title: Exercise - Block agents with security risks
points: Blocking turns off all instances created under the agent; they stay inactive until you unblock it.
Start from Overview > Agents at risk > View agents, or from the Map; open the Security tab to review risk signals.
Select Block, enter a reason and description, then Save.

units.title: Exercise – Use rules and automate agent management
points: Agent management rules apply bulk governance and lifecycle actions at scale (Agents > Settings > Agent management rules).
Default rules: install Microsoft agents; reassign ownerless Agent Builder agents to manager; block agents confirmed compromised.
Review the Pending agents tab, select Run, then check Processed agents.

units.title: Manage tools
points: Agent tools include AI-powered tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; plugins package skills and MCP connectors.
Use common MCP servers or bring your own (BYO) remote MCP server (preview) and register it with Agent 365.
Unmanaged tools risk unauthorized data access, excessive permissions, unapproved third-party integrations and compliance violations.
Registry tab: view tools and publishers, block or unblock; Requests tab: review, approve or reject user requests.

units.title: Exercise - Activate and manage tools
points: Agents > Tools: the Registry shows tool, plugin and MCP server totals; an MCP server has Overview, Tools and Policies tabs.
Policies can be enabled or disabled for Path Access, Query Limits, Collection Limits and Mutations.
Approving a requested MCP server is followed by consenting to its Microsoft Entra permissions; only then is it available to agent building surfaces.
Blocking an MCP server or plugin stops agents using it; a blocked plugin stays registered and visible.

units.title: View audit logs
points: Microsoft Purview audit records show who approved an agent, what it accessed and how it behaved, similar to user auditing.
Uses: monitor who creates, changes or deletes agents; prove compliance; investigate incidents; set alerts on agent events.
Path: agent > Security tab > Microsoft Purview protections > Review, then in the Microsoft Purview portal Audit > Search with a date range and search name.

keyTerms.definition: A bundle of Entra, Purview, Defender and SharePoint policies applied to an agent at activation or publication; default or custom.
Microsoft Entra entitlement that grants an agent identity access to resources with approvals, time limits and access reviews.
Publishing makes an agent available in the store for chosen users; activating approves users to create instances of it.
Prebuilt rules that apply governance actions in bulk, such as reassigning ownerless agents or blocking compromised ones.
Model Context Protocol server giving agents a standard interface to data, actions and business logic; governed in Agents > Tools.

tables.title: Request states in the Requests tab
rows: Waiting for admin review before publishing to the store
Waiting for approval before users can create instances
An update awaits review before being published

remember: Policy **templates** secure the agent; **access packages** control what resources its identity can reach.
**Block** = all instances off until unblocked; **delete** = agent not required; **assign owner** = missing information.
AI Administrator can use access packages but needs more roles for **Conditional Access** (and **Attribute Assignment Administrator** for custom security attributes).

selfCheck.q: You want only the Procurement team to see and use agents in the store during a pilot. Which setting?
selfCheck.a: Agents > Settings > User access, set to Specific users and groups and add the Procurement group.

selfCheck.q: Dozens of agents built with Agent Builder have no owner. How can you fix this at scale?
selfCheck.a: Run the Agent management rule that reassigns ownerless Agent Builder agents to the manager (review Pending agents, then Run).

selfCheck.q: A user requested a BYO MCP server. After you approve it, what is still needed before agents can use it?
selfCheck.a: Consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions the MCP server requires; it is available to agent building surfaces only after consent.

modules.title: Monitor and optimize Microsoft 365 AI services
modules.learnSummary: Learn why Microsoft 365 offers several Microsoft Copilot and agent report sources, choose the right one for a given question, reconcile Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Foundry costs without double-counting, and use Microsoft 365 Service Health and Copilot controls to diagnose AI-service issues honestly.
modules.tldr: Microsoft 365 splits Copilot and agent reporting across several surfaces, so you must pick the right report, state its population and freshness, and never treat usage counts as ROI. The module also covers reconciling Microsoft 365 and Foundry costs without double-counting, AI FinOps optimization, and using Service Health with the Copilot Control System pillars to diagnose issues.
objectives: Select the correct report source to answer a specific Microsoft Copilot or agent adoption, productivity, or ROI question.
Read the Copilot usage report and the separate Agent usage report to distinguish licensed access from actual adoption.
Reconcile Microsoft 365 AI services costs across the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Cost Management.
Apply AI FinOps practices—workload selection, model cost tiers, consumption reduction, and cost attribution—to optimize Microsoft 365 AI spend.
Use Microsoft 365 Service Health and the Copilot Control System's three-pillar governance model to monitor AI-service health and recommend admin actions that improve adoption.
keyPoints: **Route by question**: admin center for licensing and basic activity, Copilot Dashboard or Viva Insights for adoption and work patterns, Purview Audit for events, Copilot Studio and Foundry for their own agents; Agent 365 for the agent estate.
**Enabled users** is a licensing figure; **active users** tried a user-initiated Copilot feature. Active divided by enabled is the active users rate.
The **Copilot Agents usage report** replaces the deprecated agent report: licensed and unlicensed users, about 1 hour latency; SharePoint agents used in Teams are excluded.
Usage counts are **not** productivity, value or ROI; work-pattern comparisons are **impact indicators**, not proof of causation.
**Cost systems differ**: Microsoft 365 uses credits and policies; Foundry uses Azure meters. The same tagged charge (such as `m365copilotchat`) seen in both is booked **once**.

**AI FinOps**: manage spend, optimize value, allocate deliberately. Cheapest saving is not automating at all; deterministic work needs no model; match **basic, standard, premium** model tiers to the task.
Heavy consumers are not automatically a problem: check for **proportionate value** before restricting; attribute spend with group-scoped policies, named cost owners, showback or chargeback.
**Service Health** is incident evidence only; Copilot controls have three pillars: security and governance, management controls, measurement and reporting.

units.title: Pick the right report source for a Microsoft Copilot adoption question
points: Two valid numbers can differ because platforms, populations, periods or freshness windows differ; state those premises first.
Copilot Studio agents, Foundry deployments and other "agents" report through different surfaces despite the shared name.
Roles: AI Administrator views Copilot reports; Insights Analyst plus Viva Insights licensing for Advanced Insights; Audit Reader or Audit Manager for Purview Audit.
Dashboard day-level metrics can trail up to 2 days and week-level up to 6; Copilot-assisted hours and value are estimates.
Copilot audit records use RecordType and Operation CopilotInteraction; they don't guarantee verbatim prompt text and appear within about 30 minutes to 2 hours.

units.title: Exercise - Pick the right report source
points: Active users over 28 days: Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot (AI Administrator).
Work-pattern change: Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights; align data-through dates and name alternative explanations.
Who did what, when, in which app: Purview Audit (CopilotInteraction); an empty result means no matching event for those filters only.
Copilot Studio agent analytics versus Foundry usage and cost (Monitoring Reader, Cost Management Reader) are different reports.

units.title: Read the Microsoft Copilot usage report and the Agent usage report
points: Copilot usage report is typically available within 48 hours after the UTC day ends; timeframes 7, 30, 90 or 180 days; the previous 3 days are revalidated and can shift slightly.
