Enabled Users counts licensed people; Active Users counts those who used a feature; total prompts submitted covers Copilot Chat.
"Edit with Word" counts toward chat prompts but Excel and PowerPoint equivalents don't, so per-app prompt counts aren't directly comparable.
Current Copilot Agents usage report (Reports > Usage > Copilot > Agents): declarative, SharePoint and custom engine agents, about 1 hour latency; Reports Reader is enough.

units.title: Exercise - Read the Microsoft Copilot usage report and the Agent usage report
points: Gap calculation: 20 enabled minus 11 active = 9 licensed users inactive (55% active rate); a starting point, not a cause.
Per-app breakdown shows where adoption is strongest or weakest; app counts overlap.
Agent report offers 7 and 30 day windows (the 28-day Copilot window isn't compatible); compare only when definitions, population, UTC bounds and filters line up.
An empty report means no in-scope usage visible, not zero consumption or cost.

units.title: Reconcile Microsoft Copilot and agent costs across surfaces
points: Microsoft 365 Copilot > Cost Management: AI Administrator or License Administrator manage policies and limits; Global or Billing Administrator set billing methods.
A limited spending policy stops access to governed services for the rest of the month and resets on the first of the next month; it doesn't reserve credits.
Funding order: capacity packs, then P3 prepaid credits, then pay-as-you-go; overview refreshes every 4 hours; billed amounts update daily.
Foundry costs come from Azure Cost Management (Cost Management Reader); don't mix actual and amortized cost; Azure budgets notify, they don't stop resources.
Book duplicate views of the same tagged charge once; allocate shared cost by project tag or an agreed basis totaling 100%; use tokens per accepted work as an efficiency indicator.

units.title: Exercise - Reconcile Microsoft Copilot and agent costs across surfaces
points: Confirm period, currency and actual cost basis match before combining.
Scenario: USD 120 Microsoft 365 charge (seen twice, booked once) plus USD 100 Foundry (80 model + 20 storage) = USD 220; double-counting would give USD 340.
Unattributed USD 25 split by accepted summaries 60/40 (USD 15 and USD 10).
A worse tokens-per-accepted-summary ratio is something to investigate, not proof of inefficiency.

units.title: Optimize AI spend across Microsoft 365 AI services
points: AI FinOps stages: manage spend, optimize value, allocate deliberately.
Score use cases 1 to 5 on business impact, technical feasibility and user desirability; deterministic work should use conventional logic; pilot the hardest step first.
Credit cost depends on model, context, tools and runtime; Copilot Studio rates are basic, standard and premium, and reasoning models trigger an extra premium generative AI tools charge.
Govern environments (exploration, test, funded production) and audit the estate to retire unused agents.
Study heavy users' value before restricting; scope policies to groups, use separate subscriptions or resource groups, name cost owners; showback reports, chargeback bills.

units.title: Assess AI-service health with the Copilot Control System
points: Health > Service health (Service Support Administrator or Helpdesk Administrator); history covers 30 days; planned maintenance is in Message center; no posted issue doesn't prove health.
Three pillars: security and governance; management controls (licensing, agent lifecycle, spending limits); measurement and reporting.
Diagnose before acting: state metric and data-through time, name at least two explanations, check Service Health, then pick one scoped action with a follow-up metric.
An organizational message fixes only an awareness gap, not license, incident, latency, workflow or quality problems.

keyTerms.definition: Active Users divided by Enabled Users in the Copilot usage report; shows what share of paid seats is actually used.
An observed relationship in work-pattern data that does not prove Copilot caused the change.
Practice of connecting what AI costs to what it produces and acting on the gap: manage spend, optimize value, allocate deliberately.
Showback reports each team's consumption without moving money; chargeback bills it to the team's own subscription.
Admin center view of Microsoft incidents and advisories relevant to the tenant; evidence of incidents only.
Governance model with three pillars: security and governance, management controls, measurement and reporting.

tables.title: Which report answers the question?
rows: License readiness and basic Copilot activity
Copilot Dashboard or Viva Insights Advanced Insights
Foundry monitoring and Azure Cost Management

tables.title: Model cost tiers
rows: Advanced content creation, document and image processing

remember: Enabled users = **licenses**, active users = **behavior**; neither proves value or ROI.
Same tagged charge in Microsoft 365 and Azure → **one charge, book once**.
Deterministic task (lookup, rule) → **no model at all**; routine task → basic tier, not premium.
No Service Health issue posted → **absence of evidence**, not proof the service is healthy.

selfCheck.q: A compliance investigator needs to know who triggered one Copilot interaction and in which app. Which source?
selfCheck.a: Microsoft Purview Audit (CopilotInteraction record), with an Audit Reader or Audit Manager role.

selfCheck.q: A small group of users consumes most Copilot credits. What is the best first step?
selfCheck.a: Check whether they produce proportionate value; if so spread their practices, otherwise coach them or apply a targeted limit, not a blanket restriction.

selfCheck.q: Copilot adoption looks flat this month. What should you do before sending an organizational message?
selfCheck.a: Diagnose: note the metric and data-through time, check Service Health, license eligibility and latency, name at least two explanations, then choose a scoped action with a follow-up metric.
